text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Immigrants living in Sweden are on average registered as committing twice as many crimes as people born in Sweden, according to a new report by a crime group and the centre for immigrants.

- For the first time in 40 years the afternoon newspaper Expressen is no longer the country's biggest seller. Rival tabloid Aftonbladet has taken some of its readership and is now bigger with 382,000 readers daily against Expressen's 369,400.
- Volvo Truck closes its U.S. factory in Ohio at the cost of 700 million crowns, cutting the result for the third quarter.
- Pressure increases for Sweden to link the crown to the ERM with Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer saying a link to ERM is necessary before joining EMU.
- Continuing resignations in Sweden's health service shows the discontentment in the service. Two more doctors have left in a protest about cuts in funding and staff.

- Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink criticises European Union spending policies. He said Sweden may not want to join EMU if that meant spending even more on EU agricultural subsidies and a top-heavy administration.
- Foreign investors have taken an interest in the 24,000 square metre Kista Shopping Centre outside Stockholm owned by Wasa insurance company with several calls about its sale.

- Volvo Trucks third quarter results are expected to come in at zero after the vehicle manufacturer decided to close down its plant in Orville, Ohio. The closure will cost 700 million crown and 500 employees will be laid off.
